title: Deduplicate Rows with ROW_NUMBER
description:
The `customers` table has duplicate rows for some customers (same `email`, different `id`). Keep only the **row with the lowest id** per email, removing all duplicates.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`, `city`, `country`

Output columns: `id`, `name`, `email`. Order by `id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com','New York','USA'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com','London','UK'),(3,'Alice Dup','alice@example.com','Chicago','USA'),(4,'Carol','carol@example.com','Paris','France'),(5,'Bob Dup','bob@example.com','Berlin','Germany');
solution_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT id, name, email, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM customers) SELECT id, name, email FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY id
hints: PARTITION BY email groups duplicates; ORDER BY id ASC gives the earliest row rn=1.
Filter WHERE rn = 1 to keep only the first occurrence.
explanation: ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by email and ordered by id assigns 1 to the row with the smallest id in each email group. Filtering rn=1 keeps only that row, effectively deduplicating.
